narrative: Across April–May 2026 the agent-assistant repo was built up through a long sequence of agent-relay DAG/supervisor workflows that spec, implement, harden, and review v1 packages of a TypeScript-first assistant SDK (originally `@relay-assistant/*`, renamed mid-stream to `@agent-assistant/*`). Early sessions established canonical specs and a v1 backlog under `docs/specs/` and `docs/architecture/` (core, sessions, surfaces, connectivity, coordination, routing, traits, memory), then implemented each as an isolated package under `packages/<name>/` using a recurring 3-agent pattern: lead-claude (plan) → implement-codex (code+tests) → review-claude/review-codex (verdict). Hardening passes followed each implementation when reviewers flagged gaps (connectivity, coordination, post-audit cleanup), and a major rename workflow (`rename-relay-assistant-to-agent-assistant-sdk-workflow`, 1h37m) plus a remediation pass swept package names and public docs. Later sessions shifted into the `@agent-assistant/harness` package: a deepagents-style port adding `createSubagentToolRegistry` (task tool), `createPlanningToolRegistry` (write/list/complete_todos), and `createScratchpadToolRegistry` (scratch_read/write/list/edit) under `packages/harness/src/{subagent,planning,scratchpad}-registry.ts`, each with its own design doc, vitest suite, fix-tests/fix-regressions repair loops, and lead-review gate, capped by an `aa-08-typecheck-and-lint` workflow and a `0.9.0` version bump + PR body session. The most recent v0.5–v0.7 harness improvement workflows (`docs/specs/v0.5-harness-improvements.md`) added direct provider model adapters (anthropic/openai/gemini), opt-in parallel tool batches with terminating results, `transformTranscript` fallback, evidence-density payload typing, trace flush/settlement resilience, and subpath export wrappers — and notably found v0.5 already green, choosing not to churn source. Other threads added `@agent-assistant/vfs` as a provider-neutral VFS contract + CLI (and fixed the publish workflow to build it before artifact copy), `@agent-assistant/memory` raw helpers for relay-backed scoped retrieval and latest-session promotion, and a librarian VFS enumeration with `apiFallback` source diagnostics. A separate proactive-signals master workflow ran two waves in parallel: wave 1 added `packages/proactive/src/quiet-hours.ts` and `signal-inbox.ts`; wave 2 added `packages/surfaces/src/slack-presence-signal.ts` and `github-signal-source.ts` classifiers with tests and index re-exports.

decisions.question: Workflow shape for the Ricky one-shot harness implementation
decisions.chosen: Pipeline pattern with deterministic gates and explicit repair loops
decisions.reasoning: Task is linear with bounded implementation slices; pipeline minimizes coordination overhead while preserving hard validation checkpoints
decisions.impact: Repair-from-evidence loop avoids speculative edits when first-pass is green

conventions.pattern: Supervisor workflow: lead-claude (plan) → implement-codex (code+tests) → review-claude/review-codex (verdict) with verification-based completion markers (e.g. `V1_<X>_REVIEW_COMPLETE`)
conventions.rationale: Separates planning, execution, and review responsibilities and produces auditable artifacts in `docs/architecture/`
conventions.scope: Every v1 package workflow (core, sessions, surfaces, connectivity, coordination, routing, traits, memory) and harness ports

conventions.pattern: Per-package layout under `packages/<name>/` as TypeScript-first, isolated, with its own `package.json`, `src/index.ts` re-exports, vitest suite, dist build, and design doc in `packages/<name>/docs/` or `docs/architecture/`
conventions.rationale: Allows packages to be runnable and testable in isolation and published independently

conventions.pattern: Spec-then-implement cycle: author `docs/specs/v1-<area>-spec.md` and `docs/architecture/v1-<area>-implementation-plan.md` before code; reconcile when canonical specs change
conventions.rationale: Keeps implementation traceable to spec and supports reconciliation workflows when specs drift
conventions.scope: All v1 packages and the v0.5–v0.7 harness improvements

conventions.pattern: Repair loops: `fix-typecheck` → `fix-tests` → `fix-regressions` → `lead-review` after every impl step
conventions.rationale: Tightens 80-to-100 validation; lead-review gates catch regressions before merge
conventions.scope: aa-* harness workflows (subagent, planning, scratchpad registries, typecheck/lint)

conventions.pattern: DAG with parallel waves and convergence barriers (e.g. wave1 quiet-hours + signal-inbox, wave2 slack-presence + github-signal)
conventions.rationale: Maximizes throughput when slices are independent; barriers ensure build/test stability before next wave

conventions.pattern: Acceptance criterion: skip source edits when broker evidence shows BUILD_EXIT=0 and TEST_EXIT=0
conventions.rationale: Avoids speculative churn and respects the deterministic gate contract
conventions.scope: Repair-from-evidence steps in Ricky harness workflows

lessons.lesson: Publish workflows must include all packages in the dependency-aware build order, not just the publish matrix
lessons.context: The runtime-core publish matrix included vfs but the build-order step omitted it, so artifact upload failed copying packages/vfs/dist before it existed
lessons.recommendation: When adding a new package to the publish matrix, also add it to the build-order list and to CI validation; assert dist existence pre-copy

lessons.lesson: Marker-based completion can be noisy — prefer verification-based completion with explicit exit codes and signals
lessons.context: Many workflow steps emit STEP_COMPLETE legacy markers mixed with terminal output; later steps switched to verification-based completion (file changes + exit=0)
lessons.recommendation: For new workflows, drive convergence off verification evidence (file mutations, command exit codes, sentinel strings) rather than printed markers

lessons.lesson: Long lead-plan steps can balloon to 60+ minutes of model time
lessons.context: `lead-audit-plan`, `lead-coordination-hardening-plan`, and `lead-plan` runs each took ~1h while implement/review steps stayed under 10m
lessons.recommendation: Cap planning steps with a tighter prompt or smaller model; planning shouldn't consume more wall clock than implementation

lessons.lesson: Reviewers will flag follow-ups even on PASS verdicts — schedule a hardening pass per area
lessons.context: Connectivity, coordination, and post-audit reviews all returned PASS_WITH_FOLLOWUPS that became dedicated `harden-v1-*` workflows
lessons.recommendation: Bake a hardening slot into the program plan after each implement workflow rather than treating it as ad-hoc

lessons.lesson: Renames need a remediation workflow because reviewers find blocking residuals
lessons.recommendation: For repo-wide renames, plan a same-day remediation workflow tied to the review verdict before declaring the rename done
